sections.heading: SI Units & Prefixes
points: Base SI units: Mass (kg), length (m), time (s), current (A), temperature (K), amount of substance (mol).
Derived units: Express any derived unit in base units using equations (e.g. 1 N = 1 kg m s-2, 1 J = 1 kg m2 s-2, 1 V = 1 kg m2 s-3 A-1).
Standard prefixes: femto (f, 10-15), pico (p, 10-12), nano (n, 10-9), micro (μ, 10-6), milli (m, 10-3), kilo (k, 103), mega (M, 106), giga (G, 109), tera (T, 1012).

sections.heading: Errors, Uncertainties & Precision
points: Random errors: Unpredictable variations; reduced by taking repeat readings and calculating a mean.
Systematic errors: Consistent offset (e.g. zero error); affects accuracy, not reduced by repeats.
Percentage uncertainty: %U = (absolute uncertainty / measured value) × 100%. For repeated readings, absolute uncertainty is half the range.
Combining uncertainties: Add absolute uncertainties when adding or subtracting; add percentage uncertainties when multiplying or dividing; multiply %U by power n when raising to power n.
Graph gradients: Uncertainty in gradient = (mmax - mmin) / 2 using steepest and shallowest lines of worst fit through error bars.

sections.heading: Constituents of the Atom & Specific Charge
points: Specific charge: Ratio of charge to mass (Q/m) in C kg-1.
Strong nuclear force: Repulsive below ~0.5 fm, attractive between ~0.5 fm and ~3 fm, negligible beyond 3 fm.
Alpha decay: A decreases by 4, Z decreases by 2; Beta-minus decay: neutron → proton + e- + ν̅e.

sections.heading: Particles, Antiparticles & Photons
points: Photon energy: E = hf = hc/λ.
Pair production: Photon with E ≥ 2E0 converts into a particle-antiparticle pair.
Annihilation: Particle + antiparticle → two photons moving in opposite directions, each with Emin = E0.

sections.heading: Particle Classification & Quantum Phenomena
points: Hadrons (feel strong force): Baryons (3 quarks, e.g. p = uud, n = udd; proton is the only stable baryon) and Mesons (quark-antiquark, e.g. pions, kaons).
Leptons (fundamental): e-, νe, μ-, νμ; lepton number Le and Lμ are conserved separately.
Photoelectric effect: hf = Φ + Ek(max). Threshold frequency f0 = Φ/h; intensity affects photoelectron rate, not Ek(max).
de Broglie wavelength: λ = h/p = h/(mv), demonstrated by electron diffraction.

sections.heading: Progressive & Stationary Waves
points: Wave equation: c = fλ; phase difference Δφ = 2πΔx/λ.
Polarisation: Only transverse waves can be polarised; demonstrates oscillations are perpendicular to energy transfer.

Stationary waves: Formed by superposition of two progressive waves of equal frequency/amplitude travelling in opposite directions. Nodes (zero amplitude), antinodes (max amplitude); distance between adjacent nodes = λ/2.
First harmonic on a string: f = (1 / 2L) √(T / μ).

sections.heading: Refraction, Diffraction & Interference
points: Snell's law: n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2; refractive index n = c / cs.
Total internal reflection: Occurs when n1 > n2 and θi > θc, where sin θc = n2 / n1.
Young's double-slit: Fringe spacing w = λD / s (valid when s « D).
Diffraction grating: d sin θ = nλ; maximum order nmax = ⌊d / λ⌋.

sections.heading: Vectors, Kinematics & Newton's Laws
points: SUVAT (constant acceleration): v = u + at, s = ½(u+v)t, s = ut + ½at2, v2 = u2 + 2as.
Projectiles: Horizontal velocity vx is constant; vertical motion has a = g downward.
Moments & equilibrium: Sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments; resultant force = 0.
Momentum & impulse: p = mv; F = Δp/Δt; impulse FΔt = Δ(mv) = area under F-t graph.

sections.heading: Work, Energy, Power & Materials
points: Work & power: W = Fs cos θ; P = ΔW/Δt = Fv; efficiency = useful power out / total power in.
Hooke's law & elastic energy: F = kΔL; Eel = ½FΔL = ½k(ΔL)2.
Young modulus: E = tensile stress / tensile strain = (FL) / (AΔL), gradient of linear stress-strain graph.

sections.heading: Current, Potential Difference & Resistivity
points: Definitions: I = ΔQ/Δt, V = W/Q, R = V/I, P = IV = I2R = V2/R.
I-V characteristics: Ohmic conductor (straight line through origin), filament lamp (curves as T rises → R increases), diode (conducts above ~0.6 V forward bias).
Resistivity: ρ = RA/L (in Ω m). Superconductors have zero resistivity below critical temperature Tc.

sections.heading: Circuits, Potential Dividers & Internal Resistance
points: Kirchhoff's laws: Conservation of charge at junctions (ΣIin = ΣIout); conservation of energy in loops (Σϵ = ΣIR).
Internal resistance: ϵ = I(R + r) = V + Ir; terminal p.d. V = ϵ - Ir (gradient = -r, y-intercept = ϵ).
Potential divider: Vout = Vin × R2 / (R1 + R2); used with thermistors (NTC) and LDRs for sensing circuits.

3.6.title: Topic 3.6 · Further mechanics and thermal physics

sections.heading: Circular Motion & Simple Harmonic Motion
points: Circular motion: ω = 2πf = v/r; centripetal acceleration a = v2/r = ω2r; centripetal force F = mv2/r = mω2r.
SHM defining equation: a = -ω2x; x = A cos(ωt), vmax = ωA, amax = ω2A.
Oscillators: Mass-spring T = 2π√(m/k); simple pendulum T = 2π√(l/g). Resonance occurs when driving frequency = natural frequency.

sections.heading: Thermal Physics & Ideal Gases
points: Specific heat & latent heat: Q = mcΔθ; Q = ml.
Ideal gas equation: pV = nRT = NkT (T in Kelvin, T(K) = θ(°C) + 273.15).
Kinetic theory: pV = (1/3)Nm(crms)2; mean KE per molecule = (3/2)kT = (3RT)/(2NA).

sections.heading: Gravitational & Electric Fields
points: Newton's law & field strength: F = GMm/r2; g = F/m = GM/r2; Vg = -GM/r (work done per unit mass from infinity).
Orbits: T2 = (4π2/GM)r3; escape velocity v = √(2GM/R); geostationary orbit has T = 24 h above equator.
Coulomb's law & electric field: F = Q1Q2/(4πϵ0r2); E = F/Q = V/d (uniform) = Q/(4πϵ0r2) (radial); Ve = Q/(4πϵ0r).

sections.heading: Capacitance & Magnetic Fields
points: Capacitors: C = Q/V = Aϵ0ϵr/d; energy E = ½QV = ½CV2; time constant τ = RC; Q = Q0e-t/RC.
Magnetic forces: F = BIL sin θ; F = BQv sin θ (circular radius r = mv/(BQ)).
Electromagnetic induction: Φ = BA; NΦ = BAN cos θ; Faraday's & Lenz's laws: ϵ = -Δ(NΦ)/Δt; transformer Vs/Vp = Ns/Np.

sections.heading: Radioactivity & Nuclear Radius
points: Inverse-square law for gamma: I = k/x2.
Exponential decay: A = λN, N = N0e-λt, T1/2 = ln(2)/λ.
Nuclear radius: R = R0A1/3 (where R0 ≈ 1.05–1.2 fm), meaning nuclear density is constant and independent of A.

sections.heading: Mass-Energy, Fission & Fusion
points: Mass-energy equivalence: ΔE = Δmc2; 1 u = 931.5 MeV.
Binding energy: Energy required to separate a nucleus into its constituent nucleons; Fe-56 has the highest binding energy per nucleon.
Fission & fusion: Thermal neutrons induce U-235 fission; moderator slows neutrons, control rods absorb neutrons, coolant transfers heat.

sections.heading: Telescopes & Astronomical Classification
points: Refracting telescope (normal adjustment): M = fo/fe; length = fo + fe. Suffers from chromatic and spherical aberration.
Cassegrain reflecting telescope: Parabolic primary mirror + convex secondary mirror; avoids chromatic aberration.
Resolving power: Rayleigh criterion θ ≈ λ/D. CCDs have ~70-80% quantum efficiency vs ~4% for the eye.
Magnitudes & spectra: m - M = 5 log(d/10); Wien's law λmaxT = 2.9 × 10-3 m K; Stefan's law P = σAT4; H-R diagram & OBAFGKM spectral classes.

sections.heading: Cosmology
points: Doppler shift: Δλ/λ ≈ Δf/f ≈ v/c (for v « c).
Hubble's law: v = Hd; age of universe ≈ 1/H.
Evidence for Big Bang: Cosmological redshift, CMBR (2.7 K blackbody), primordial H/He abundance; Type 1a supernovae as standard candles reveal accelerating expansion (dark energy).

sections.heading: The Eye, Ear & Biological Measurement
points: Eye & lenses: Power P = 1/f (dioptres); myopia corrected with diverging lens, hypermetropia with converging lens; rods (scotopic) vs cones (photopic/colour).
Ear & intensity: Intensity level dB = 10 log10(I/I0) where I0 = 1.0 × 10-12 W m-2.
ECG: P wave (atrial depolarisation), QRS complex (ventricular depolarisation), T wave (ventricular repolarisation).

sections.heading: Imaging Techniques
points: Ultrasound: Piezoelectric transducer; acoustic impedance Z = ρc; reflection coefficient = ((Z2 - Z1)/(Z2 + Z1))2; coupling gel matches impedance.
X-rays & CT: Attenuation I = I0e-μx; mass attenuation μm = μ/ρ; CT scans produce 3D cross-sections using rotating X-ray fan beam.
MRI & Tracers: MRI uses Larmor precession of hydrogen protons in strong B-field; PET/gamma camera uses Technetium-99m (6 h half-life, pure gamma).

sections.heading: Rotational Dynamics
points: Moment of inertia: I = Σmr2; rotational KE = ½Iω2.
Torque & angular momentum: T = Iα; angular momentum L = Iω (conserved when external torque = 0); rotational power P = Tω.
Flywheels: Store rotational kinetic energy to smooth torque fluctuations or provide high power bursts.

sections.heading: Thermodynamics & Engines
points: First law of thermodynamics: Q = ΔU + W, where W = pΔV at constant pressure.
Isothermal & adiabatic: Isothermal (T constant, pV = const); Adiabatic (Q = 0, pVγ = const).
Engine cycles & efficiency: Indicated power = area of p-V loop × cycles/s; ηmax = (TH - TC)/TH; COPref = TC/(TH - TC).

sections.heading: Discovery of the Electron & Wave-Particle Duality
points: Thomson's e/m experiment: Crossed E and B fields give v = E/B; magnetic deflection gives e/m = E/(rB2).
Millikan's oil drop: Balances weight mg = QV/d to show electric charge is quantised in multiples of e = 1.60 × 10-19 C.
Electron microscopes: TEM uses magnetic lenses for high resolution (λ = h/√(2meV)); STM uses quantum tunnelling current across a narrow gap.

sections.heading: Special Relativity
points: Michelson-Morley experiment: Null result showed no luminiferous aether and that c is invariant.
Postulates: Laws of physics are identical in all inertial frames; speed of light c is constant for all observers.
Relativistic effects: Time dilation t = t0/√(1 - v2/c2), length contraction l = l0√(1 - v2/c2), relativistic mass m = γm0, E = mc2 = E0 + Ek.

sections.heading: Discrete Semiconductors & Operational Amplifiers
points: Op-amp ideal properties: Infinite open-loop gain, infinite input impedance, zero output impedance, infinite bandwidth.
Inverting amplifier: G = -Rf/Rin; Non-inverting amplifier: G = 1 + Rf/R1; Summing amplifier: Vout = -Rf(V1/R1 + V2/R2 + ...).
Comparator & MOSFET: Op-amp comparator saturates to ±Vs; MOSFETs act as voltage-controlled switches with high input impedance.

sections.heading: Logic Gates, Timing & Data Communication
points: Logic & Boolean algebra: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR; De Morgan's laws: (A·B)̅ = A̅ + B̅ and (A+B)̅ = A̅·B̅.
Sequential circuits: SR and D-type flip-flops; astable and monostable timing circuits.
Data transmission: Sampling theorem (fs ≥ 2fmax); AM vs FM modulation; optical fibres and multiplexing (TDM/FDM).
